Subject: Re: Data retention baseline for hosted inference (clarification request)

Hi Asha — appreciate the note and the urgency. Below is a concise, pragmatic summary of Redwood's current hosted defaults and options; I'll attach the retention matrix and our SOC2 summary for your procurement/security review.

Summary (hosted API defaults):
- Raw request payloads (verbatim prompts + metadata): retained by default for 30 days. This window supports debugging, replay, and fraud/abuse investigations.
- Streaming tokens / intermediate fragments: treated as part of the request stream and retained for up to 24 hours unless captured as part of a final stored transcript.
- Final model outputs (full generated text/files): retained by default for 90 days as "derived outputs" to support quality regressions, evals, and customer support.
- KV cache artifacts and ephemeral model state: considered transient and not persisted to durable storage by default; caches are kept in GPU memory and short-lived disk-backed caches expire within hours.
- Aggregated telemetry & billing logs: stored for 365 days for auditing and billing reconciliation (no PII included).

Options for protected data:
- No-store mode: available for hosted customers (adds minimal latency tradeoffs). When enabled, Redwood configures the account so verbatim request/response content is not written to persistent logs. Ephemeral caches still exist in-memory for serving but are not persisted.
- Private deployment / VPC: for customers who must keep all data in a customer-managed VPC or on-prem, Redwood provides the Private offering (customer controls retention).

Residency:
- By default hosted accounts are pinned to a region at creation. For Nimbus we recommend US‑region pinning (us-west-2) — replicas for disaster recovery are kept within US regions only unless you request cross-region replication.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a short retention matrix. If you need formal wording for the questionnaire (one‑paragraph statements per row), say the word and I'll send an exportable table.

Asha — attaching the files we discussed: SOC2-type2_Q4_2027_summary.pdf and a retention matrix that maps each artifact type to default retention and available options.

Two action items we can take immediately if Nimbus wants tighter controls:
1) Turn on account-level "no-store" (we'll provision the flag and confirm via security addendum). If chosen, Redwood will not persist verbatim request/response content to durable logs (retention windows for billing/aggregates remain intact).
2) If you require enforced US-only residency with no cross-region copies, we can bind your tenant to the us-west-2 region and include a residency clause in the MSA/addendum.

Next steps: please confirm which option you prefer and I'll route the security addendum for signatures (DocuSign link included in the Drive export). If you'd like, Karthik can run a short tech session on how "no-store" affects observability and debugging workflows.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a call today if helpful.

Best regards,
